title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Anthropic swell lifts the Nasdaq lineup
conditions.summary: Futures are bouncing hard, led by tech, as Anthropic prepares its record Nasdaq debut and Palo Alto Networks pops on earnings. Yields near 5% and hawkish Fed talk keep it from being epic.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: S&P 500 futures are up about 1% and Nasdaq-100 futures about 2% in early trading; Dow futures are up about 0.6% and Russell 2000 futures about 0.5%.
The 10-year Treasury yield is about 5.07%, slightly lower; the dollar index closed Wednesday near 103.9, up 0.4% (no fresh overnight quote found).
WTI crude is up about 0.6% near $83 on Middle East shipping tensions; gold is slightly lower near $3,730; bitcoin is down about 1.4% near $63,600.
The VIX is down about 10% to roughly 22 after Wednesday's jump.
Asia: the Nikkei ended slightly higher, Hong Kong and Shanghai slipped, and Australia's ASX fell about 1% after a weak October jobs report.
Europe: coming off a third straight losing session on Wednesday, when the Euro Stoxx 50 fell about 1% and miners led losses.
Wednesday's close: Dow -1.1%, S&P 500 -0.2%, Nasdaq Composite +0.4%.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: 7:30 AM CT: Weekly jobless claims, consensus about 198,000 (prior 200,000).
7:30 AM CT: Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index, consensus about 21 to 23 (prior 20.9).
9:00 AM CT: Leading economic index, expected flat; 10:00 AM CT: Kansas City Fed manufacturing; noon CT: 10-year TIPS auction.
Fed speakers (CT): Hammack about 7:50 AM, Jefferson 8:25 AM, Goolsbee 11:30 AM, Barr 1:15 PM; Barkin later in the day (sources differ on the time).
October Fed minutes showed nearly all officials see further rate hikes as likely, keeping December hike talk alive.
Trump met Xi and Putin at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, with trade, chip export controls and Strait of Hormuz shipping on the agenda.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Palo Alto Networks beat: adjusted EPS $1.05 vs $0.97 expected and revenue $3.44B vs $3.31B, with guidance above estimates and a $4.5B Applied Compute deal; shares up about 10% pre-market.
Before the open: Walmart (consensus about $0.64 EPS on $187B revenue), Alibaba, PDD Holdings and NetEase.
Tencent's quarterly revenue came in below expectations, and its US-listed shares slipped.
After the close: Intuit; also reporting today are Ross Stores, Keysight, Williams-Sonoma, Gap, Elastic and Bath & Body Works.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: ANT (Anthropic): IPO priced at $83, above the $70-$78 range, raising about $81B at roughly a $1.5T valuation; trading starts today on Nasdaq, with gray-market indications 20% or more above the offer.
PANW (Palo Alto Networks): +10% — earnings beat, raised outlook and Applied Compute acquisition.
MU (Micron): +4.7% — chip stocks rally with Nasdaq futures.
INTC (Intel): +4.5% — first external customer for its 18A process and an expanded Microsoft supply deal.
MRVL (Marvell): +4% and AMD: +3% — semiconductor rebound.
NVDA (Nvidia): +1.8% — Trump said Blackwell chip sales to China could be allowed in two to three years, after a five-day losing streak.
SLS (Sellas Life Sciences): about -20% — discounted $150M stock offering after a positive leukemia trial readout.
BABA (Alibaba): about -0.6% — near a 22-month low on new US data-center curbs, ahead of earnings.

sections.title: Business News
items: Anthropic's roughly $81B raise is the largest IPO on record, topping SpaceX's $75B listing in June.
Moody's cut its outlook on Nvidia to stable from positive, citing governance after the CEO leadership shakeup, while affirming the Aa1 rating.
The Justice Department said it is willing to clear more mergers with behavioral commitments instead of asset sales, pointing to the Fox-Roku deal.
TSMC and Samsung reportedly paused some chip shipments to Chinese customers while seeking US licenses (Samsung detail unconfirmed).
OpenAI's CEO said the company still plans to go public.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 7:30 AM CT jobless claims and Philly Fed, with the 10-year yield sitting near 5%.
Anthropic's opening trade on Nasdaq and whether it pulls the rest of AI tech along or drains money from it.
Walmart's results and outlook for a read on the holiday shopper, plus Fed speakers through the day.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Thursday, November nineteenth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. Riding shotgun on the board is my first mate, Gus the wonder dog. Give the beach a howdy, Gus! The swell. After a choppy Wednesday, futures are rolling in clean. S and P 500 futures are up about one percent. Nasdaq 100 futures are up about two percent. The Dow and the Russell are up about half a percent. The ten year yield is near five point oh seven percent. Crude is up slightly near eighty three dollars, gold and bitcoin are a bit lower, and the VIX is down about ten percent. Tokyo edged higher, Hong Kong and Australia slipped, and Europe is coming off three down days. The big wave: Anthropic priced its initial public offering at eighty three dollars a share, raising about eighty one billion dollars, a record. It debuts on the Nasdaq today. That's one big grom paddling out. Wind and weather. At seven thirty A M Central we get jobless claims, expected near one hundred ninety eight thousand, and the Philadelphia Fed factory index. Five Fed speakers hit the beach today, and the latest minutes showed most officials see more rate hikes ahead. Tide chart. Palo Alto Networks beat on earnings, raised its outlook and announced a deal for Applied Compute. The stock is up about ten percent. That calls for a treat, Gus! Here you go, buddy! Walmart and Alibaba report before the open, Intuit after the close. The lineup. Chip stocks are stoked. Micron is up near five percent and Marvell about four. Intel is up about four and a half percent on a new chipmaking customer and a bigger Microsoft deal. Nvidia is up nearly two percent on hopes for future China sales. Wipeout: Sellas Life Sciences is down about twenty percent after a discounted stock sale. Gnarly. Beach talk. Moody's trimmed its outlook on Nvidia, citing governance. And the Justice Department says it may clear more mergers without forcing asset sales. Sets to watch: the seven thirty data, Anthropic's first trade, and whether the Nasdaq can hang ten with yields near five percent.
